 LeBron and the Sixers Headline NBA Weekend Primetime Action
 By Lovette Ochicha - November 21, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp 
 One of the NBA’s hottest teams takes centre stage at a fan-friendly time on Saturday as LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers welcome Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks at 7 p.m. WAT, live on SportyTV.
 The Sixers have established themselves among the league’s early pace-setters, topping the Eastern Conference with 13 wins and three losses.
 Philadelphia will be monitoring Jaylen Brown’s availability after he missed the team’s last game against Orlando with a hamstring injury.
 Head coach Nick Nurse said Brown would be evaluated once the Sixers return from their road trip. Senegal’s Tacko Fall will also be hoping for another opportunity after making the most of 10 minutes against the Magic on Wednesday night, recording an impressive three blocks.
 Much of the spotlight, however, will be on 22-time NBA All-Star LeBron James, who continues to rewrite the NBA record books in his unprecedented 24th season.
 At 41, James is extending his record for the most seasons played in NBA history and adding another chapter to a career spanning more than two decades.
 His presence alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe gives Philadelphia a formidable mix of experience and star power.
 Saturday’s meeting is also a rematch of Philadelphia’s 127-116 victory over Milwaukee on Oct. 24, when Joel Embiid recorded a triple-double with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.
 LeBron James missed that contest, while Jaylen Brown contributed 27 points. Led by 2025 NBA All-Star Tyler Herro, who is averaging 19.4 points per game, Milwaukee will look to end a 12-game losing streak.
 The NBA action continues on Sunday when the Detroit Pistons visit the Atlanta Hawks at 9:30 p.m. WAT, live on ESPN. Detroit enters the weekend at 10-4 and has won four of its last five games, led by Cade Cunningham, who is averaging 25.8 points and 7.8 assists per game.
 Atlanta is 9-6 and comes into the weekend on a two-game winning streak, including a 117-112 road victory over Oklahoma City. Both teams are playing in the Emirates NBA Cup tonight, before facing each other on Sunday.
 Nickeil Alexander-Walker leads Atlanta in scoring at 21.2 points per game. In his seventh season with the Hawks, Onyeka Okongwu is averaging 15 points and 8.2 rebounds per game.
 Fans across Africa can catch Philadelphia vs. Milwaukee on Saturday, 21 November at 7 p.m. WAT on SportyTV, followed by Detroit vs. Atlanta on Sunday, 22 November at 9:30 p.m. WAT on ESPN.
